title: Los Angeles Unified Launches Ed, a Pioneering Learning Acceleration AI Platform
supports_claim: LAUSD stated that Ed analyzed district data including grades and attendance to recommend resources and was launched first at selected schools.
limitations: District launch announcement is first-party and describes intended design and claimed controls, not independently verified effectiveness or safety.

title: LAUSD moves ahead with troubled AI effort despite collapse of host firm
supports_claim: The report states that LAUSD disabled the Ed chatbot after learning that vendor AllHere had laid off most employees, illustrating vendor-continuity risk.
limitations: Secondary reporting; it does not establish a technical root cause, quantify student harm, or independently audit the district's data protections.

title: AI writing detection model release notes
supports_claim: Turnitin acknowledges possible false positives, suppresses numeric scores from 1 to 19 percent, and says an AI score should not be the sole basis for adverse action.
limitations: Vendor-authored and updated over time; performance claims are not an independent audit and model behavior can differ by language, version, text length, and population.

title: Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text
supports_claim: The study tested commercial and public detectors and concluded that no easy reliable detection solution exists and that educators should focus on preventive assessment design.
limitations: The test corpus and tools were time-bounded, mainly English-language, and vendors knew some documents were part of a test; findings may not generalize to later versions.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Teaching and Learning: Insights and Recommendations
publisher: U.S. Department of Education Office of Educational Technology
supports_claim: The report recommends centering people, equity, safety, effectiveness and transparency when adopting AI in education and retaining humans in instructional loops.
limitations: Non-binding U.S. policy guidance from May 2023; examples are not endorsements and it does not classify UniTutor under Vietnamese or EU law.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework AI RMF 1.0
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports_claim: NIST provides a voluntary Govern-Map-Measure-Manage framework for managing AI risks across design, deployment, use and monitoring.
limitations: Voluntary and sector-agnostic; using the framework does not demonstrate legal compliance or prove any UniTutor control is effective.

title: Luật Trí tuệ nhân tạo số 134/2025/QH15
supports_claim: The official record states that Vietnam AI Law 134/2025/QH15 was issued on 2025-12-10 and took effect on 2026-03-01.
limitations: A legal reviewer must apply the full statutory text and implementing instruments to the final intended purpose, vendor role, data flow and deployment facts.

title: Luật Bảo vệ dữ liệu cá nhân số 91/2025/QH15
supports_claim: The official record states that Vietnam Personal Data Protection Law 91/2025/QH15 was issued on 2025-06-26 and took effect on 2026-01-01.
limitations: This source establishes the law and dates but is not a completed data-protection impact assessment for UniTutor's exact processing operations.

title: Quyết định 33/2026/QĐ-TTg ban hành Danh mục hệ thống trí tuệ nhân tạo có rủi ro cao
publisher: Thủ tướng Chính phủ Việt Nam
supports_claim: The official record confirms a Vietnamese high-risk AI system list effective from 2026-08-15, requiring intended-purpose review rather than inference from a generic risk score.
limitations: The landing page alone does not resolve whether a non-grading study tutor falls within a listed category; counsel must review the attached decision and deployment facts.

title: AI Act regulatory framework and risk-based approach
supports_claim: The Commission explains that education systems affecting access or learning outcomes may be high-risk and that chatbots must disclose that users are interacting with AI.
limitations: The page is an evolving overview rather than tailored legal advice; classification depends on intended purpose and the final AI Act text and applicable guidance.

title: iTutorGroup to Pay 365000 Dollars to Settle EEOC Discriminatory Hiring Suit
supports_claim: EEOC reported a settlement involving automated screening that allegedly rejected applicants based on age, supporting a cross-industry lesson against unreviewed adverse decisions.
limitations: Settlement of an employment allegation is not an admission or technical finding and the system was hiring automation, not an education tutor.
